newsitem.title: USA: AT&T withdraws U.S. satellite license plan.
newsitem.headline: AT&T withdraws U.S. satellite license plan.

text.p: AT&T on Thursday said it withdrew its application with the U.S. Federal Communications Commission for a license to launch a new generation of geostationary communications satellites.

In a statement, AT&T said investment in the new Ka-band satellite technology was a capital-intensive initiative that did not fit with its new strategy. Ka-band refers to radio frequencies that handle two-way voice and data communications.
It said the move was based on plans to concentrate on businesses central to its core businesses in growth areas such as wireless, online and local services.

"We are focusing on our core business and some growth areas, and satellites is not core to that," AT&T spokesman Gary Morgenstern said, adding that the company was not withdrawing from satellite operations completely.
In particular, he said the company continues to offer direct broadcast satellite services through its minority stake in Hughes Electronics Corp's Direct TV venture.
AT&T's Ka-band project was formally known to the industry as the AT&T VoiceSpan Satellite System.
The satellites would have allowed AT&T to offer a range of next-generation, broadband communications, including voice, video and Internet services.
The company said about 50 employees were engaged in the VoiceSpan project and that it would attempt to reassign them.
The decision to withdraw the new application reflects a general retreat from satellite operations by AT&T and follows the disposal of several non-core businesses in recent months.
In April, General Electric Co's GE Spacenet unit agreed to buy AT&T's Very Small Aperture Terminal satellite operations for an undisclosed amount.
